# ddns-updater-installer

Installs [qdm12/ddns-updater](https://github.com/qdm12/ddns-updater) on Windows from a single PowerShell command - DuckDNS only

## Install

1. Open PowerShell.
2. Copy the command below and paste it into PowerShell.
3. Press Enter. Approve the Windows UAC prompt if asked to create the background service.

<!-- BEGIN WINDOWS INSTALL COMMAND -->
```powershell
$p=''; $t=Join-Path $env:TEMP 'ddns-updater-installer.ps1'; [IO.File]::WriteAllText($t,[Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String($p)),[Text.UTF8Encoding]::new($false)); try { & powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$t" } finally { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $t -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
```
<!-- END WINDOWS INSTALL COMMAND -->

The command writes the encoded installer to a temporary file, runs it with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, and removes the file when it finishes. You do not need to download the script or change your machine's execution policy.

## What the installer does

- Downloads the latest Windows release from GitHub and verifies its SHA-256 checksum.
- Prompts for your DuckDNS domain and token, then writes `data/config.json` with entries that maintain both the IPv4 (A) and IPv6 (AAAA) records.
- Installs into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\DDNS-Updater` by default.
- Registers a `DDNSUpdater` Windows service that starts automatically at boot and restarts if it fails.
- Adds Start menu shortcuts for running, updating and uninstalling.
- Adds an entry to **Apps & features** / **Add or Remove Programs**.
- Adds the install directory to the current user's `PATH`.

## Update and uninstall

Use the **Update DDNS Updater** and **Uninstall DDNS Updater** shortcuts in the Start menu. Both remain available after the initial install.

The update shortcut also offers to regenerate `data/config.json` (the previous file is backed up first), so configuration changes such as IPv6 support can be applied to an existing install. Answer `y` to apply them, or just press Enter to keep your current configuration.

## Regenerating the encoded command (developer note)

After editing `install-windows.ps1`, run:

```powershell
pwsh ./encode-installer.ps1
```

This replaces the text between the README markers. Use `pwsh ./encode-installer.ps1 -Check` to verify the README is current.
